title: Austin's New Planning & Zoning Experts
summary:
*   Austin's City Council held a special meeting to address critical urban planning and zoning needs.
*   Council members discussed the urgent need to appoint new experts to the city's planning and zoning bodies, as several current members were unable or unwilling to continue serving.
*   An interim Planning Commission was established, comprising nine primary members and five ex-officio advisors, appointed to guide city development until June 1st.
*   The City Manager was directed to draft the official ordinance required to formalize these planning commission appointments.

Discussion was held on appointing an interim board to keep the work moving, until the new
Council came in. It was also pointed out that it was necessary to have someone who was
familiar with zoning and planning rather than getting someone that would have to educate
himself along these lines.
Some of the members of the Planning Board and Zoning Commission had wanted to resign, and
some had stated they could not serve.

Councilman White moved that those nine persons be asked to serve as a Planning Commission
until June 1st, and that the other five be asked to serve as ex-officio members of that
Commission to sit, advise and study with them.
The motion, seconded by Councilman Johnson, carried by the following vote: Ayes:
Councilmen Johnson, Long, MacCorkle, White, Mayor Drake Noes: None Councilman Johnson
